notes: The decision to help the White Glove Society or not does not have any repercussions in the game or even when completing the quest for the Legion during Render Unto Caesar (other than gaining Legion fame and significant Karma loss. This is the only quest in New Vegas that doesn't carry any repercussions between factions, towns, locations or non-player characters. This is also one of the few quests that allows for bypassing the bulk of the quest progression and kill almost everyone in it without damaging meaningful faction reputation or Karma.

If choosing to drug the banquet wine, after the head waiter picks up the drugged wine, you can pickpocket it off him with no change in the current objective (the White Glove Society members will still become comatose).

Also, when entering the dining hall, attempting to talk to the unconscious White Gloves actually opens up their extended inventory (the clothes they are currently wearing will be listed), which can be looted without loss of Karma or reputation. Even after finishing the quest, the members will not replace their clothing or masks, and they will walk around in their underwear. Also, if one tries to wake them up when they are drugged by hitting one and then "holstering" one's fists, they all will walk around the room and can still be looted as if they were unconscious but cannot be interacted with further until one leaves.

If all the Securitrons on the Strip were killed previously, it can be difficult to finish this quest via framing Gunderson as the quest markers will simply point to empty spaces and the Securitrons can take a very long time to respawn. This can be detrimental when playing on Hardcore as you will most likely have to wait for over a week, during which time you will have to keep sleep, dehydration and hunger levels down. On the PC version accessing the console, targeting a dead Securitron and entering the command "resurrect" will restore the robot to life and allow you to complete the quest.
Mr. House will have unique dialogue if one sides with him and then completes this quest by either stopping Mortimer's plans or helping him return the Society to cannibalism.

If one chooses to frame Heck Gunderson for his son's death, the Securitron that comes to arrest him will be a Mark I, regardless of whether one upgraded the Securitron army at the Fort to Mark II for either Mr. House or Yes Man.
If you bring Ted back to Heck and then kill Heck, the White Glove Society will shun you, but Heck's hired gun will help you fight them.

Picking the lock to the door that leads to the cashier's booth will result in negative Karma, and upon approaching the cashier, he will become hostile. However, if you simply pick the lock then shut the door, there will be no resulting hostility.

Following a patch, the only way to receive Strip fame from this quest is to dissuade Heck Gunderson from imposing a food blockade, which is possible only if Ted was brought back alive to his father, thus failing Pheeble Will. Helping Mortimer gains Idolized reputation with the White Glove Soceity but has no effect on one's Strip reputation. (It's also possible to just kill Ted and lie to Heck that he was found but don't know who did it, which will also grant Strip fame as well as White Glove fame).

As of version 1.4, neither Mortimer nor Marjorie's dialogue options about cannibalism or Ted Gunderson will appear until an offer is made to Heck to find his son, making talking to Heck the only way to start the quest.

The option to offer up a human companion to Mortimer as a substitution serves as the only way outside of Hardcore mode for them to be permanently killed without changing one's reputation with any other factions that might result in them turning hostile and becoming non-essential.

On the "hostile NCR" failure path, it is possible to prevent the appearance of NCR Ranger hit squads when failing this quest by becoming Idolized with the NCR beforehand. In fact, so long as nothing else is done to antagonize the NCR, it is possible to breach the El Dorado substation and get them to agree to a truce with the Brotherhood of Steel during Wild Card: Side Bets without dropping NCR reputation below Idolized. They will even still accept help in preventing President Kimball's assassination during You'll Know It When It Happens.

By doing this, it is also possible to gain the rewards for helping Eddie (300 XP instead of the normal 200), only become shunned (Powder Ganger camps will not attack the player character) by the Powder Gangers (See Notes) and gain the reputation increase with the NCR. First, betray Eddie to Hayes. Then, instead of talking to Lee outside of the prison, head on in. Speak to Eddie prior to killing him and let him know about the attack, stealth kill him and equip NCR faction armor (armor optional), then run outside and through the visitor's center to speak with Lee as he is running (from the left) inside. Keep running after speaking to him and over the ridge if one lacks NCR faction armor. He will reward only NCR reputation and not Powder Ganger infamy, as the latter would normally occur at this point but does no due to turning the quest in first to Eddie. Similarly, the player character gains the 300 XP for the NCR completion even though the quest is finished by Eddie.

However, if the player character uses the above method, all the NCR troopers inside the administration center will be hostile to them from that point on (even days or weeks later) if they ever enter the area without an NCR faction disguise equipped.
Powder Gangers in the scattered camps are hostile to the player character until one reputation is neutral or at least Shunned, so avoid killing them loudly to be able to speak to Eddie initially.

It is possible to talk to Eddie without a Stealth Boy, even if one is vilified by the Powder Gangers. The easiest way to do this is to kill Powder Gangers who can see through disguises (Dawes, Carter, Hannigan, bodyguards, etc), and stealthily kill all other Powder Gangers (Not necessary to kill Meyers). One may need to remove and then put the Powder Gangers faction armor back on to reset rep back to neutral, and also wait around until they no longer sense the player character, so they no longer appear as hostile. Using this technique, one can get rid of every Powder Ganger at the NCR Correctional Facility except for Eddie and Meyers. Then, every time one wants to talk to Eddie, run in and talk to him before he has a chance to get up. When dialogue ends, run out of the room so he cannot see the player character and turn hostile. One can also try to sneak behind the computer on his desk and back away.

Killing all of Eddie's guards stealthily may allow one to get to Eddie and initiate dialogue without hostilities, as a workaround for the above issue. If he becomes hostile when approached after his guards are dead, try running quickly at him and repeatedly trying to talk. If the player character gets to him before he stands up, he will talk to them. Also, one can sneak behind the computer on his desk after the talk, back away to the wall, then stand up and walk away.

If one wants to help the Powder Gangers or sit back and let the NCR and Gangers fight it out (without betraying them), it is recommended that one visits the Cell Blocks and the Visitor Center, so that more Gangers will join the battle. This will lead to a slightly more even fight.

If one wants to be certain to complete the quest, (and not intervene), one will have to visit each cell block, otherwise the NCR will just kill the Powder Gangers in the yard, then the Admin building. After Eddie is killed the NCR troops will go into idle mode and walk around the building leaving the Powder Gangers alive in other buildings. One named Powder Ganger may remain in one of the cell blocks, (a sneak kill if one wants to keep their rep intact).

The dialogue to hand over one's weapons to exit the monitoring station will only take place once and will not be repeated while still inside. This means that any weapons or aid can be stored in a container within the weather station before triggering the dialogue, then grabbed before exiting the building, with no consequences.

One can also circumvent this by assassinating the door guards on the inside without initiating the dialogue, so long as they are not detected, which will allow the player to carry their weapons back to Caesar's tent.

If one wants to work with the NCR but has worked with Yes Man for too long, e.g. by progressing Wild Card: Side Bets with a few minor factions, Don't Tread on the Bear! will automatically begin. At this point, if one completes one more quest for Mr. House or Yes Man, that quest will fail and permanently lock out the NCR ending.

An alternative route can be done where Janet can be lied to in her first interaction by passing a 55 Speech check, telling her that she is expected at the base and that it's safe to go to Jack before arranging for her to do so safely. Failing the check results in her knowing that she is being lied to, asking if the player character is trying to get her killed, and will also fail the quest.

If Janet was killed by the bombardment, Jack can always be found sleeping at the Nellis workshop afterward. When talked to, he will be furious and ask why the Courier did not stop her. After being lied to with a 35 Speech check that she risked everything for him, he will "curse the walls of Nellis" and go back to sleep. If the check was failed, or one tells him it's not their fault she died, Jack will refuse to talk to them afterwards.
